title: Call: Red Cross Wants a Shelter at Brennan County High, but the Building Has No Power

transcript.speaker: EOC Clerk
transcript.text: Brennan County EOC, recorded line.

transcript.speaker: Red Cross
transcript.text: This is Marisa Okafor, disaster program manager with Red Cross Western Kentucky. I'm calling about overnight sheltering. We want to open at Brennan County High School, since it's your first site. I need a formal request from the EOC before I move anyone or anything. We're planning for 150 to 200 people from Corwin and the Clarks River parks.

transcript.speaker: Red Cross
transcript.text: Here's the problem. Ashford Municipal Utilities says the high school's feeder is down, and that building has no backup generator. Without power there's no heat, no lights and nowhere to charge oxygen concentrators. It's dropping into the low forties out there. I'm not putting people in a dark gym. So I need two things from you: the request, and an answer on power.

transcript.speaker: EOC Clerk
transcript.text: Hold on, ma'am. The superintendent just texted the EOC. It came in at 00:51. Quote: 'My custodian can unlock BCHS in 30 minutes once I have the EOC's request in writing. Who is bringing the generator, and who pays for the fuel?' End quote.

transcript.speaker: Red Cross
transcript.text: Yeah. That's the question. I can have a trailer rolling out of Paducah with cots, blankets, water and breakfast. I can't bring a generator big enough to run that gym and the boiler. Somebody on your side has to find one, whether that's county stock or a state request. I'll hold the trailer until I hear who's bringing it and when.

transcript.speaker: EOC Clerk
transcript.text: The Health Department duty nurse is on the other line. I'm adding her to the bridge now.

transcript.speaker: Health Dept Nurse
transcript.text: This is Carla Whitfield, duty nurse. We know of at least four oxygen users from Shady Acres and Riverbend, and two dialysis patients due for treatment Saturday morning. The out-of-state caller's father at Shady Acres lot 22 is one of the oxygen users. His portable tank won't last much longer. I need a medical needs corner at the shelter with working outlets, and a list of who's coming in so I can match my staff to it.

transcript.speaker: Red Cross
transcript.text: Carla, I'll give you a corner by the gym doors if there's power at the wall. Without it you've got oxygen users and nothing to plug into.

transcript.speaker: EOC Clerk
transcript.text: One more thing, for the record. The BrennanAlert console at 00:54 shows template POST-03, BWN 4, message type 3, post-storm safety and shelter information, English and Spanish, ready to send. Reachable exchanges: Ashford, Central, South, East. Unreachable: Corwin, Pine Hollow, Riverbend, Shady Acres.

transcript.speaker: Red Cross
transcript.text: So the people we're opening this shelter for won't get the text. Who tells the north end where to go, and when? Give me the request, a power answer and an opening time I can put on my end. Call me back at this number. I'll be by the phone.

voiceStyles.Red Cross: Woman in her 50s, experienced and direct, steady, sounds like she's in a moving vehicle
voiceStyles.Health Dept Nurse: Woman in her 40s, clinical and quick, a little out of breath, phones ringing behind her

instructorNote: Core decision point for sheltering after the storm. Watch whether the EM Director formally requests the BCHS shelter through the EOC under EOP 3.3, gets Schools to open the building, has the Deputy find a generator (county stock or a request to the state), and has the Health Department staff a medical needs area. Also watch whether the Warning Officer sends POST-03 in English and Spanish only once the opening time is confirmed. For the north end, players should route the message through Channel 6, radio and Sheriff vehicle PA, and should not send a county WEA: a post-storm shelter is not a permitted county WEA use under BWN 5, and the north-end towers are down anyway.
